title: Keepers of Velocity: All-Hands Huddle
summary: Quarter-end all-hands focused on velocity, resourcing for Q1 initiatives, and an operational runbook for fallbacks and private deployments. Leadership covered hiring cadence adjustments, a brief reliability postmortem, and introduced a new cross-functional "keepers" program to reduce coordination friction.
topics: Q4 outcomes and signal-to-noise on priorities
Private deployments & compliance posture (SOC2 / SAML / KMS)

Marcus: validate Dedicated autoscale behaviour with a synthetic throughput test and share raw logs (due 2026-01-08)
Sophie: update hiring forecast & candidate pipeline dashboard, flag critical roles (ongoing)

transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-12-17 17:00 UTC
- Duration: ~64 minutes
- Attendees (not exhaustive): Elena Park, Ravi Desai, Leah Morgan, Marcus Li, Sophie Grant, plus ~120 on the all-hands call

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Leadership gives Q4 readout, we do quick incident retrospective, announce "keepers" program to reduce handoffs, talk hiring and priorities for Q1. A couple of questions on compliance and private deploys; some audio dropouts around 00:42 mark.

---
00:00 - Elena: "Hey everyone, thanks for being here. Uh, quick housekeeping, we'll run about an hour, a little more maybe. We're not reading a big deck today, it's more signal and next steps. Ravi, kick us off with the ops piece?"
00:21 - Ravi: "Yeah, thanks. So overall Q4 numbers are, uh, pleasing. Throughput per GPU up ~13% month over month. That said we had a multi-region event last week — our failover plan executed but there was a 7-9 minute window where some folks saw increased tail latency and a small chunk of requests hit the fallback model. We have logs and traces in the Console, uh, it's in the incident channel. Quick note: some of the telemetry postmortem references 'K V cash' — that's a transcription artifact, it's KV cache."
00:45 - Leah: "I missed that bit, is the incident because of routing or infra saturation?"
00:53 - Ravi: "Routing + a bad edge condition in the smart routing policy where concurrent requests spiked on a particular host. Autoscale did not bring capacity fast enough because of an internal back-off; also the canary rollout we had for a kernel change amplified things in region-eu. So two things collided."
01:18 - Marcus: "Right, the kernel rollout had a lower perf regression at 1k tokens for a variant; we should tighten our perf gate there. I think we didn't have a strong enough perf delta threshold. Action: I'll put a new perf gate in CI."
01:35 - Elena: "Okay but overall the customer impact was limited?"
01:38 - Ravi: "Yes, limited — about 0.2% of total requests during the window, but it shows fragility. We should treat it like an early-warning signal, not a bad day."

02:05 - Elena: "On the strategic front — quick hiring update. Sophie?"
02:12 - Sophie: "Hiring's moving but slower. We have offers out for two infra SWE roles and one product engineer. Time-to-hire drift is about 22 days longer than target across the board. Comp is competitive but the pipeline needs more volume. We want managers to prioritize interview slots and mark roles as critical in the tracker."
02:33 - Elena: "This feeds directly into velocity. If we have gaps, squads can't take on the batch of Q1 initiatives. Leah, what's the product top-three for Q1?"
02:41 - Leah: "Three things: 1) Redwood Optimize pilot rollouts — automated quantization and config suggestions for PLG workloads; 2) Private deployments GA for a subset of enterprise customers with KMS + audit logs; 3) Streaming latency improvements — better batching heuristics and prefix cache hits."
03:06 - Audience question (typed): "Will Private GA require VPC peering or will we support VPN?"
03:11 - Leah: "Both will be supported, but initial GA will be VPC peer and customer-managed KMS for key material. We will have an options doc. There's also a compliance checklist — SOC2 is green, a few docs for SAML integrations remain. Note: some sellers heard 'sack two' in the draft, that's just S O C 2 in the transcript."

03:45 - Ravi: "On the private deploys note: the private control plane will be opt-in, and for on-prem we have an air-gapped package but that has longer lead time. We'll need SEs to work with security teams for cert rotations and H S M/K M S integration."
04:10 - Marcus: "Engineering will carve out a small team for the on-prem installer, but I want to avoid long-lived forks. We'll keep the runtime the same and package deploy recipes."

04:35 - Elena: "We're also introducing the 'keepers' program. The idea: nominate a small group per cross-functional area — reliability, onboarding, SDK DX, cost tooling — who are empowered to shepherd small operational changes end-to-end so that we reduce thrash. Marcus, can you frame it?"
04:49 - Marcus: "Sure, keepers are not managers. They're doers who own follow-through. For example, a keeper for 'batching & cache' will own the config defaults, coordinate with runtime, product, and SEs, and be point on any live incidents. They'll have a small time allocation. It's basically decentralizing ops accountability."
05:15 - Elena: "We expect each keeper to be assigned to 2-3 quarters of work. Sophie will own nomination and onboarding."
05:24 - Sophie: "Yes, please send nominations by end of next week. We'll hold a one-hour workshop to align responsibilities."

05:40 - Audience: "Will keepers be compensated differently or is this part of existing scope?"
05:44 - Sophie: "Mostly within current scope; if workload becomes more than 0.2 FTE we'll discuss banding and recognition. We'll treat it as a career growth path too."

06:05 - Elena: "Back to product — Leah, a quick note on Redwood Optimize: customer feedback shows config suggestions reduced token cost by ~12% but in some long-tail prompts quality dropped. How do we guard against regressions?"
06:22 - Leah: "We will tie Optimize suggestions to eval suites and a canary prompt set. If quality dips by more than the threshold we'll hold the suggestion. Also adding a rollback flag in the Console."
06:40 - Ravi: "And from infra we can add a shadow traffic check where suggestions are tested in prod-like envs before wide rollout."

07:05 - Marcus: "One operational ask: SEs, when you run benchmarks please include raw traces and the tpu/gpu kernel variant in the spreadsheet. It is painful otherwise."
07:18 - AE (unlabeled, audio): "Noted — we'll standardize benchmark templates and link them in the Incident runbook."

07:35 - Elena: "Quick finance signal: unit economics look okay but Q1 burn needs discipline. We want better cost introspection per route and token class. Cost tooling folks, please prioritize the per-route token breakdown in Console."
07:51 - Leah: "That's on the backlog for data team. We'll push it up."

08:10 - Audience crosstalk for 30s with muting/unmuting; some folks say congrats on outreach in EMEA."

08:45 - Elena: "Okay, incident follow-up: Ravi, what are the concrete o.k.r. changes?"
08:50 - Ravi: "Add a perf gate in CI for kernel changes; lower the autoscale back-off thresholds; and schedule a synthetic soak for the EU region weekly. I'll share the runbook draft by end of next week."
09:12 - Marcus: "Also I want to start a weekly 'latency clinic' with platform folks where we review tail-latency charts."
09:22 - Elena: "Good. Leah, you'll own the quality guards for Optimize. Marcus & Ravi pair on the perf gate. Sophie drives keeper nominations. I'll share the Q4 highlights and the big picture ask: fewer partially done things, more completed customer outcomes."

09:45 - Audience question: "Is there any change to Dedicated vs Hosted pitch? Customers ask about latency vs cost tradeoffs."
09:52 - Leah: "No change in pitch; we need clearer playbooks. Dedicated is for predictable throughput and data isolation; Hosted remains our fast path. We'll create a short one-pager for GTM with decision criteria."
10:10 - Sophie: "And we'll include a pointer to the new compliance matrix — SAML, KMS, SOC2 status — in that one-pager."

10:32 - Ravi: "One more technical note — there's some confusion in field about quantization profiles. We should expose recommended profiles by workload class in the Console. That will reduce support tickets."
10:45 - Leah: "Agreed, we'll add that to the Optimize roadmap."

11:00 - Elena: "Alright, lightning round for shout-outs and risks. Marcus?"
11:05 - Marcus: "Shout-out to infra on the failover work; risk: hiring slower than plan."
11:10 - Sophie: "Shout-out to onboarding ops; risk: year-end holiday scheduling."
11:14 - Ravi: "Shout-out to SE triage team, they did a good job; risk: we need to fix our canary perf gates."
11:22 - Leah: "Product PMs — great work on Optimize pilots; risk: regression on long-tail prompts."
11:28 - Elena: "Ok thanks. Final ask: everybody who is nominated as a keeper please accept the calendar invite and complete a 15-min pre-read before the Jan workshop. We're leaning into operational ownership, not more meetings."

11:48 - Audience: "Question on roadmap: any changes to regional expansion?"
11:52 - Elena: "Yes, target one new region in APAC in H1 2026, but we'll staff it carefully."

12:10 - Closing: Elena: "Thanks all, follow-up email in next 24 hours with links and action owners. Happy holidays to those who celebrate; for the rest, enjoy the break. See you in January."
